title: Serve config.js and images from /storage, seeded on first boot
description: Runtime content must survive restarts and be updatable without rebuilding the image. Plan: the server maps /config.js and /images/* to /storage (e.g. /storage/config.js, /storage/images/). An entrypoint script seeds /storage from defaults baked into the image on first boot (only if /storage is empty), then never overwrites user data. This replaces the Dropbox-symlink arrangement on the server: updating the wall = dropping new pictures + config.js into the volume. Note config.js must be served with no-cache so edits show up on reload.
acceptance_criteria: With a named volume mounted at /storage: wall renders from /storage content; editing /storage/config.js changes the wall on reload; docker rm + re-run with same volume keeps the pictures
close_reason: nginx serves /config.js and /images/ from /storage; entrypoint script seeds a fresh volume only; all three acceptance checks verified against a named volume (render, live config edit, persistence across docker rm)

title: Write multi-stage Dockerfile: CRA build + static server on port 80
description: Stage 1 (build): node image, 'npm install --legacy-peer-deps', 'NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider npm run build' (see CLAUDE.md for why both flags are needed on modern Node). Stage 2 (runtime): a small static server (nginx is the obvious pick) serving build/ on port 80, as ONCE requires. EXPOSE 80. Keep the image lean — only build/ output and server config in the final stage.
acceptance_criteria: docker build succeeds; docker run -p 8080:80 serves the wall at http://localhost:8080
close_reason: Multi-stage Dockerfile + .dockerignore + nginx.conf; acceptance checks green (build from dirty tree, 200s on /, /config.js, bundle; no Node in final image)

title: Deploy polaroid-wall on ONCE (once.com)
description:
Package the wall as a ONCE-compatible Docker container and deploy it with 37signals' once tool (https://github.com/basecamp/once).

ONCE contract (confirmed against basecamp/once README):
- container serves HTTP on port 80
- /up endpoint returns success when ready
- anything that must survive container restarts lives in /storage (that volume is what gets mounted and backed up)
- deploy = push the image to a registry and give once the image path during 'curl https://get.once.com | sh' setup

App-specific wrinkles: public/config.js is a symlink to Dropbox and public/images is untracked, so runtime content (config + pictures) must be decoupled from the baked image and served from /storage; the service worker aggressively caches the bundle, so cache headers need care.

title: Push image to a registry and install on the server with once
description: ONCE installs custom apps by image path: push the image to a reachable registry (ghcr.io or Docker Hub; decide which, and whether the image can be public — the pictures live in /storage, not the image, so the image itself holds no private photos as long as the baked seed content is a placeholder or acceptable to publish). Then on the target server: 'curl https://get.once.com | sh' and enter the image path when prompted. Afterwards, upload the real config.js + images into /storage on the server. Open questions to resolve here: which server/VPS, domain + TLS (once handles Let's Encrypt), and how to sync pictures from Dropbox to /storage (manual scp vs a small sync script).
acceptance_criteria: Wall reachable on its domain over HTTPS; /up green; pictures survive a once-driven update/restart

title: Verify the container end-to-end locally
description: Run the full ONCE-contract checklist locally before touching a server: docker run -p 8080:80 -v polaroid-storage:/storage; /up returns 200; wall renders with pictures from /storage; lazy loading still works (Network tab: only ~viewport pictures fetched, per the CLAUDE.md checklist, or the Playwright harness described there); container restart keeps content; theme switching via #Black/#White/#Colorful still works.
acceptance_criteria: All checks pass against the locally built image
close_reason: e2e/ suite (Playwright on system Chrome + docker orchestration) automates the full checklist: /up, fresh-volume seed, content from /storage byte-for-byte, lazy loading, no overlaps, themes, stop/start and rm+rerun persistence. 8/8 green against the locally built image, repeatedly. Committed as c0ae910.

title: Tame the service worker: cache headers for sw.js, config.js, index.html
description: CLAUDE.md documents that the CRA service worker serves a stale bundle after every rebuild (hence the incognito-window advice). In production that would mean deploys don't show up. Fix at the server: no-cache/must-revalidate on service-worker.js, index.html and config.js; long immutable cache on the hashed static/ assets. Consider whether to keep the SW at all (unregistering it is a valid outcome — decide and document).
acceptance_criteria: After rebuilding the image with a visible change and restarting the container, a normal (non-incognito) browser shows the new version on reload
close_reason: Unregistered the SW (src/index.js calls unregister()); nginx headers already in place since ho9.1. Verified: Playwright transition test (old visitor converges to new bundle, registrations drop to 0; fresh visitor never registers), docker build OK. Containerized e2e is ho9.5.

title: Add /up healthcheck endpoint returning 200
description: ONCE polls /up and only routes traffic when it returns success. For a static nginx server this is a location block ('location = /up { return 200 "ok"; }' or similar). Must not be shadowed by the SPA catch-all, and must not hit the service worker or filesystem.
acceptance_criteria: curl -i http://localhost:8080/up returns 200 with a small body
